title: Biomarker escalation matrix
source: Thumbprint Health Recommendation Routing Specification (#25), Section 4 and Section 9
about: Every finding routes to one lane. self = 'You can act on this' (Lane 1). provider = 'Bring this to your provider' (Lane 2). A finding is provider-lane when ANY rule in `provider` matches or any escalation condition applies; otherwise it takes `default_lane`. Thresholds are Thumbprint's, written by Dr. Locker's team; they are not guideline cut-offs. Signed off by Dr. Adam Locker, acting medical director, Oct 21 2026.
comparison: Each rule names one bound or two. gte/gt/lte/lt are numbers in the marker's unit. A value of "lab_high" or "lab_low" means the limit printed on the member's own lab report.
corrections: hs-CRP: spec #25 Section 4 prints its thresholds as 3.0 and 10.0 mg/dL. hs-CRP is reported in mg/L, and Section 2 (ESC-06), the Lane 1 range and the PhenoAge spec all use mg/L, so this matrix uses 3.0 and 10.0 mg/L. Confirmed by Adam Locker, Oct 18 2026.

Self-care ranges are guideline-based (conventional reference ranges), not functional or optimal ranges: Adam Locker's decision, Oct 19 2026. They match the Thumbprint targets table. Provider thresholds are unchanged.

levels.flag: Provider lane: prepare the member and open a 30/60-day follow-up loop.
levels.immediate: Provider lane now: the member should arrange a provider evaluation.

triggers.ESC-01: Value crosses the provider threshold in this matrix.
triggers.ESC-02: Worsening across two or more consecutive draws despite logged self-lane actions.
triggers.ESC-03: The indicated next step is a prescription.
triggers.ESC-04: A genetic or pharmacogenomic finding raises the risk of self-management.
triggers.ESC-05: A pattern across markers suggests organ-level problems that need a workup.
triggers.ESC-06: The marker is never self-managed (provider-only category).

emergency.about: Critical values, decided Oct 19 2026 (Adam Locker). Any of these bypasses the lanes and the agents and shows the hard-coded message. 'today' = contact your provider today; 'this_week' = book a visit this week. Either way, red-flag symptoms (chest pain, trouble breathing, confusion, fainting, persistent vomiting, fever) mean urgent care or the ER now. The potassium, sodium, hemoglobin, platelet and calcium cut-offs are the ones in Dr. Locker's Aug 2026 clinical rules spec, Section 7; INR over 4.5 confirmed by Dr. Locker on Oct 18 2026 (hospital conventions sit at 4.5 to 5.0). It applies to every member, with no blood-thinner gate: members upload reports from any lab, and an elevated INR in someone not on an anticoagulant is the bigger red flag.

Worsening across draws

provider.why: Likely acute inflammation: provider evaluation required.

Raised together with other inflammatory markers
Persistently above 3.0 mg/L despite supplement changes

provider.why: Significant elevation: provider to evaluate B12, kidney function and inherited methylation disorders.

MTHFR C677T homozygous and not responding

egfr.name: eGFR
egfr.default_lane_note: Provider lane by default whenever a declining trend is detected, even above 60. Self lane gives supportive guidance only (hydration, protein intake, blood pressure).

conditions.when: Any declining trend
eGFR declining with creatinine rising: nephrology consideration
Rising across draws
Creatinine raised with eGFR declining
Declining across draws
Albumin declining with ALT raised
Worsening across draws
On any supplement protocol that can injure the liver
ALT and AST both raised

provider.why: Marked variation in red cell size warrants evaluation.

conditions.when: Worsening across draws
RDW raised with abnormal WBC and low ferritin

wbc.name: White blood cell count

conditions.when: WBC and hs-CRP both raised

wbc.notes: 6.0-8.0 during an infection or stress is a self-lane note, not an escalation.

vitamin_d_25oh.name: Vitamin D, 25-OH
vitamin_d_25oh.self_range_evidence: Emerging. The 2024 Endocrine Society guideline advises against routine 25-OH-D testing and against targeting a specific level in healthy adults under 75; show that position next to this range.

provider.why: Severe deficiency: provider may recommend prescription repletion.

conditions.when: Below 20 ng/mL, where prescription repletion is the indicated step
Genetic report shows a VDR variant affecting vitamin D metabolism

provider.why: Severe iron deficiency: provider to investigate the cause.

conditions.when: High ferritin: provider to evaluate the cause
Very low ferritin with low RDW and low WBC
Worsening across draws
At a level where statin therapy is clinically considered
ApoB and Lp(a) raised with a family history of heart disease

lpa.name: Lp(a)

conditions.when: Always: genetically fixed, lifelong, and its management needs a provider

lpa.notes: Any detectable elevation warrants provider awareness. Many labs report Lp(a) in nmol/L, which does not convert reliably to mg/dL; match on the unit the lab printed.
